findings.obligation: E4 ("A completed run that had no planned repos shows no repos-read line at all, rather than a zero or placeholder count") is declared over the queue, and the queue renders the repos-read line at TWO sites: the verified-account site (queue.rs:652-653) and the no-account imports-only head (imports_only_summary, queue.rs:313-318, reached from completed_summary at queue.rs:339 via QueueHead::NoAccount). A declared behaviour needs an executable stimulus and assertion at the site that implements it; passing production code and green checks do not establish oracle coverage.
findings.observation: Measured by reading the oracle bytes and the fixture authority, not inferred. The candidate's plan-less scenario (tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs:180 a_run_kept_before_scan_plans_were_stored_says_nothing_about_repos_read) runs on rra_world_on_v1_store, and tests/fixtures/review-app-store-v1/README.md records that fixture as "Priya signed in, verified github.com/priyaraman" — an owner WITH a verified account, so the page it asserts is rendered by the verified-account site, not by imports_only_summary. The other two S2 scenarios call given_owner_verified(&world, Account::Priyaraman), also the verified site. The only test anywhere that exercises imports_only_summary asserts its SOME arm ("No GitHub account to re-check · 1 repo read", review_app_repos_and_accounts_imports.rs:365, which I ran: exit 0, 22 passed). Consequence, stated as a concrete counterexample: if the new None arm were wrong — if it kept the segment and rendered "No GitHub account to re-check · 0 repos read", or rendered a bare "· repos read" — nothing in the candidate oracle, nothing in the seven acceptance targets I ran, and nothing in the unit suites I ran would fail. The arm is reachable in production: an owner with no GitHub account but imports (D-RRA-8) whose latest completed run has no scan_run_repos row, which scan.rs reaches through the plan.is_empty() path into ended_reading_nothing (scan.rs:481-483) when her only import is skipped or removed. This is why it is NON-BLOCKING: the original Request names only the other site ("the queue shows repos_read_message for any completed run (views/queue.rs:651-653)"), so the oracle is complete against the Request as written; the uncovered arm is a correct extension the port-type change compelled, carried without an observation.
findings.remediation: Add one scenario to tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs: a signed-in owner with NO GitHub account whose latest completed run has no scan_run_repos row opens her queue, and assert her summary is exactly "No GitHub account to re-check · N new suggestions" — i.e. that the page holds neither "repos read" nor "repo read" — with the same discriminators the existing plan-less scenario uses (pin the page as a completed run's queue and pin her kept suggestions) so the absence cannot pass vacuously. Keep the existing Some-arm assertion in review_app_repos_and_accounts_imports.rs as the control.

findings.obligation: A recorded test must encode the rule production actually implements. This property's declared subject is the test-fault seam's known-name set ("only_a_development_build_takes_the_test_fault_seam"), and the S1 authority (brief.md Request; architecture.md S1 public oracle, which names refuse_mark_repo_read and refuse_record_account_checks) makes two further names known. An expectation that contradicts the authority for a value its own generator can produce is a false expectation even while the suite is green.
findings.observation: Confirmed by reading both sides, with the generator domain checked arithmetically rather than assumed. crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:688 generates `value in "[a-z_]{1,24}"` and lines 692-703 assert, for every generated name other than "migrate_before_commit", that a development build parses it to Err(ConfigError::Invalid { name: TEST_FAULT_VAR, reason: "not a known test fault" }). Production at config.rs:311-318 now also returns Ok(Some(TestFault::RefuseMarkRepoRead)) for "refuse_mark_repo_read" and Ok(Some(TestFault::RefuseRecordAccountChecks)) for "refuse_record_account_checks". "refuse_mark_repo_read" is 21 characters drawn entirely from [a-z_], so it is INSIDE this generator's domain (1..=24): the property's expectation is false for a value the generator is permitted to produce, and the suite is green only because a uniform random draw over that space does not hit the exact string. I measured the green: argv 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins', exit 0, 'running 39 tests' / 'test result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.19s', no warnings. Two separate costs, both real: the property can emit a false RED on a future seed, and — the material one — it no longer protects what it claims to protect, because a regression that silently stopped honouring either new name would leave this property green. The acceptance oracle does cover both names end to end (host run on 0525e0e, exit 0, 4 passed), which is why this is NON-BLOCKING rather than a coverage blocker. Provenance: the S1 crafter raised this itself and correctly did not edit the test; I verified it independently rather than taking the report.
findings.remediation: In crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs, give the known fault names ONE owner that both sides read — e.g. a `const KNOWN_TEST_FAULTS: [(&str, TestFault); 3]` that test_fault matches over — then in the property iterate the known names expecting Ok(Some(..)) for each, and prop_assume! the generated unknown name is not one of them. That both pins the two new names and removes the false expectation; do not weaken the property to "any name may parse".

findings.obligation: P2/E5 "A completed run that had planned repos still shows its repos-read line, with the true number of repos read for that run", and the Work statement "The review app's 'repos read' line is true". The count the queue shows must be the true one for what the owner understands as her scan.
findings.observation: CLASSIFICATION of the out-of-scope item the root asked me to classify, verified in the code and NOT widened into this Request. The under-count is real and pre-existing, and it is a PRODUCT question about what the count means, not an implementation slip. Mechanism, read end to end: begin_scan always mints a new run_id (scan.rs:116 random_token()), including for a resume; resume_plan (crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs:131-133) filters the frozen plan to rows whose status is still Planned, so rows already marked 'read' are dropped from the resumed run's plan entirely; ResumedPlan::record (scan.rs:626-629) re-records those kept rows through record_plan, whose SQL inserts every row with status 'planned' (crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs:24-27); and LATEST_SCAN counts only the LATEST run's rows (scan_runs.rs:332-337). So a scan that read 1 of 3 repos, was paused for GitHub's budget, and then resumed and read the other 2 reports "2 repos read" on the completed queue, not 3 — the figure the S1 oracle's author reported seeing. This candidate neither introduces nor worsens it: on the S1 paths a refused mark leaves nothing marked read, so the resumed plan carries every repo and the count is exact, which is precisely what then_her_queue_counts_exactly asserts; and S2's change only decides whether the line appears at all. No scenario anywhere exercises the budget-paused-then-resumed count, so nothing green here contradicts this. It is therefore non-blocking for this candidate and must not reduce or widen its scope.
findings.remediation: Decide, as the promise owner, what "N repos read" means to the owner: the latest run only, or her whole scan across its resumes. If the latter, raise it as its own Request — the fix touches how a resumed run carries already-read rows (resume.rs:131-133) and how the count is aggregated (scan_runs.rs LATEST_SCAN), with its own public oracle for a budget-paused resume. Do not fold it into fix-repos-read-truthful: the user decision of 2026-11-08 settled only the refused-write and plan-less-run cases, and this candidate satisfies both.

Design quality, judged against the bound paradigm (functional, architecture.md ## Paradigm and CLAUDE.md), with the locator of each judgment. Functional core / effect shell: every rule the candidate adds is a pure total function and no decision moved into effectful code - adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs:291-299 admits(fault, write) is a total match returning Result; scan_runs.rs:170-172 repos_read_of(planned, read) is total; wiring.rs:595-605 store_faults is total over the three fault names; config.rs:311-318 test_fault is total over the seam strings. Count the outcomes before choosing the return type: ports/src/review.rs:419-423 moves the previously-conflated outcome INTO the type (repos_read: Option<usize>, None = no plan recorded, Some(0) = planned and read none), so the state the Request calls misleading is no longer representable in the port value; a native sum that already states the distinction correctly stays native, and no extra wrapper was owed. Railway: record_checks (scan.rs:364-392) now returns Result and composes with '?' instead of 'let _ ='; mark_repo_read and record_account_checks (scan_runs.rs:275-292, 328-345) compose admits_scan_write(...).and_then(...).map_err(port_error), so the refusal travels the error track to the caller. Certainty by construction, calibrated honestly: the release twins are EMPTY enums eliminated by 'match never {}' / 'match fault {}', so a release binary cannot hold either fault - that is a compiler-level exclusion on a strong-static path, now measured (R5), not a nominal wrapper; its residual bypass is named below. Semantic SSOT: the hide discriminator exists once, in the store (repos_read_of over two correlated plan counts in LATEST_SCAN, scan_runs.rs:332-337), and the view only renders what it is given (queue.rs:313-318, 652-653) - the view never re-derives 'has plan rows' and never keys on 'the count is nought', which is the rule the Request actually named. Declared inputs, not ambient reads: the fault is injected at the composition root (wiring.rs:544-552 open_capped_with_faults) into the store value, never read from the environment inside the store. Quality axes: readable (repos_read_of, admits, ScanWrite, StoreFaults::none all named for what they mean), encapsulated (scan_write_fault is a private field read only through admits_scan_write), declarative, cohesive, decoupled (ScanWrite names the write a call site is making without the call site knowing about faults). Refactoring Priority Premise, scanned level by level over the changed units: L1 none - no dead code, no magic literal, every new item carries its why; L2 the only candidate is the five-fold 'if X.is_err() { return Ended::with_status(ScanStatus::Interrupted) }' shape in scan.rs (458, 467, 480, 555, 566 plus the new 681-687), which is the idiom already established by the surrounding code for exactly this outcome and whose folding into a combinator would add an element without removing a duplicated RULE - recorded as an accepted shape, not a finding; L3-L6 none in the changed units (no anemic type, no transaction-script decision, no feature envy, no new conditional that wants polymorphism). No over-engineering: nothing was added that no promise asks for. No wrong-state-representable rule checked at runtime that the types could exclude.
